description: The stream stops abruptly for the whole response (max output tokens reached) while a call is still collecting arguments - the call never gets its own terminal event at all. This is the more common real-world shape of a length cutoff: the provider simply stops sending events, rather than sending an explicit unsafe reason on the call itself (see C03 for that variant). A call abandoned this way - never explicitly terminated at all, not even with a truncation signal - is a stronger anomaly than an acknowledged truncation and fails closed harder: reject, not retry.
